summary: Bug fix VERIFIED: When admin updates apparatus assignment personnel_ids, a notification is now created in the user_notifications collection and appears in the firefighter's notification bell dropdown with the correct title, message, link, and unread badge count. Backend (5/5 pytest passing) and frontend (Playwright UI flow) both confirm the fix end-to-end.

minor.issue: create_notification() helper in user_notifications_routes.py inserts into DB but does NOT broadcast a WebSocket 'user_notification' event. NotificationBell.js subscribes to that WS event for instant updates (otherwise it relies on 30s polling or manual dropdown open to refresh). Consider adding a manager.broadcast(...) call so the bell badge updates in real-time without polling.

passed_tests: Backend: PUT /api/apparatus-assignments/{id} with personnel_ids triggers create_notification_for_personnel; notification appears in user_notifications with title='Riding Assignment Updated', type='assignment', link='/on-duty', link_label='View On Duty', is_read=false
Backend: PUT /api/user-notifications/{id}/read marks notification as read and persists
Backend: 'pt-' prefixed personnel_ids are correctly skipped (no notification, no error)
Frontend: Firefighter login -> /dashboard renders, WebSocket connects+authenticates
Frontend: Bell badge updates from absent to '1' after admin updates apparatus assignment (verified via fetchUnreadCount call after dropdown click)

Frontend: Bell dropdown shows notification item with title 'Riding Assignment Updated', message containing apparatus name + 'Station 10' + date, 'Just now' timestamp, 'View On Duty' link label, blue unread indicator dot
Frontend: Toast notification also appears on screen (existing apparatus-update WS broadcast still works)
action_items: (Optional / Minor) Broadcast a WebSocket 'user_notification' event in create_notification() so the bell badge updates in real-time instead of waiting for 30s poll or manual dropdown open. The frontend NotificationBell.js already listens for this event (handleNotificationUpdate) - backend just needs to emit it.

(Test-data caveat) The task spec referenced 'Firefighter 100003 / firefighter123' but the seed only creates payroll 100001 (admin) and 100002 (BC); firefighter user accounts are created on-demand via /api/auth/set-temporary-password. For this test I activated personnel 200003 (Firefighter 10, Station 10, A-Shift) with password 'firefighter123'. If a literal 100003 account is required for QA, please add it in the seed.
critical_code_review_comments: staffing_routes.py update_apparatus_assignment correctly guards 'pt-' prefix and uses BackgroundTasks for non-blocking notification creation - clean implementation.

user_notifications_routes.create_notification_for_personnel correctly resolves personnel_id -> personnel.payroll_number -> users.id chain; gracefully returns None if either lookup fails (no exception thrown to caller).

NotificationBell.js useEffect deps include [isOpen] for the polling interval and a second useEffect on [isOpen] both invoke fetchNotifications when isOpen changes - functionally fine but duplicative; could be consolidated.

NotificationBell.js: useAuth import casing is '../../context/AuthContext' but WebSocket is '../../contexts/WebSocketContext' (plural) - confirmed both paths exist; consider standardising directory name.

create_notification() inserts but does not emit websocket event - real-time bell updates depend on the 30s poll. Consider broadcasting a 'user_notification' WS message scoped to the user channel for instant UX.

rca of the issue: Original bug: notification bell dropdown was empty even though toast notifications fired. RCA: update_apparatus_assignment was broadcasting a WebSocket 'apparatus_update' event (which the toast handler picks up) but was NOT inserting any record into the user_notifications collection (which the bell reads). Fix applied by main agent: added background_tasks.add_task(create_notification_for_personnel, ...) inside update_apparatus_assignment for each non-'pt-' personnel_id, with proper title/message/link/metadata. Verified: notification now persists in user_notifications, GET /api/user-notifications returns it for the assigned firefighter, unread-count increments, and the dropdown displays it on open. Remaining minor gap: create_notification helper doesn't broadcast a WS event, so bell badge update relies on 30s polling unless dropdown is opened (not blocking, but could be improved for instant UX).
